sn56.16:1.1: “Bhikkhus, do you remember the Four Noble Truths taught by me?”
sn56.16:1.2: When this was said, a certain bhikkhu said to the Blessed One:
sn56.16:1.3: “Venerable sir, I remember the Four Noble Truths taught by the Blessed One.”
sn56.16:2.2: do you remember the Four Noble Truths taught by me?” “I remember suffering, venerable sir, as the first noble truth taught by the Blessed One.
sn56.16:2.3: For if any ascetic or brahmin should speak thus:
sn56.16:2.4: ‘This is not the first noble truth of suffering taught by the ascetic Gotama;
sn56.16:2.5: having rejected this first noble truth of suffering, I will make known another first noble truth of suffering’—
sn56.16:2.7: “I remember the origin of suffering as the second noble truth taught by the Blessed One….
sn56.16:2.8: I remember the cessation of suffering as the third noble truth taught by the Blessed One…. I remember the way leading to the cessation of suffering as the fourth noble truth taught by the Blessed One.
sn56.16:2.9: For if any ascetic or brahmin should speak thus:
sn56.16:2.10: ‘This is not the fourth noble truth of the way leading to the cessation of suffering taught by the ascetic Gotama;
sn56.16:2.11: having rejected this fourth noble truth of the way leading to the cessation of suffering, I will make known another fourth noble truth of the way leading to the cessation of suffering’—
sn56.16:2.13: “It is in this way, venerable sir, that I remember the Four Noble Truths taught by the Blessed One.”
sn56.16:3.2: It is good that you remember the Four Noble Truths taught by me.
sn56.16:3.3: Suffering, bhikkhu, is the first noble truth taught by me: remember it thus.
sn56.16:3.4: For if any ascetic or brahmin should speak thus …
sn56.16:3.10: ‘This is not the fourth noble truth of the way leading to the cessation of suffering taught by the ascetic Gotama;
sn56.16:3.13: having rejected this fourth noble truth of the way leading to the cessation of suffering, I will make known another fourth noble truth of the way leading to the cessation of suffering’—
sn56.16:3.15: “In this way, bhikkhu, remember the Four Noble Truths taught by me.
sn56.16:4.1: “Therefore, bhikkhu, an exertion should be made to understand: ‘This is suffering.’… An exertion should be made to understand: ‘This is the way leading to the cessation of suffering.’”
